0.2.0.lead: From this version on, this window says what changed after every update. This time: backups to download, a way to hold back upgrades and a much smaller database.

sections.title: Backups
sections.body: nexcrate now backs itself up weekly at night, daily or monthly if you like. Every copy can be downloaded as an encrypted archive and restored later, with the key for the stored credentials.

sections.title: Hold back upgrades
sections.body: Missing movies and episodes now load before upgrades, in SABnzbd and in qBittorrent. There is also a pause for everything already there when you switch it on, and a limit per day.

sections.title: Do not upgrade what is there
sections.body: When taking over from Radarr or Sonarr and when reading folders from disk, you can tick that the files brought along stay as they are. What is missing is still searched.

sections.title: Remove several titles
sections.body: In the library you can select several titles and remove them at once, with their files moved to the recycle bin if you like.

sections.title: Anime by scene numbers
sections.body: Releases that count episodes through are now matched and searched by TheXEM's scene numbers, as in Sonarr. You can switch this off per series and set the number by hand on every episode.

small: The database is much smaller: nexcrate keeps only what it reads from TMDB and gives empty space back at the start. The first start after the update takes a few minutes longer for it.
TheXEM is only asked about series it knows, and not at all for six hours after a failure.
A file taken over during an import now counts as filed in the log.

0.3.0.lead: This version guards against the wrong movie under the right number, says why nothing was loaded, and keeps the database free while large imports run.

sections.title: The wrong movie under the right number
sections.body: Some indexers list a release under another movie's TMDB or IMDb number. nexcrate now also reads the name: a release whose name fits none of the movie's titles is never taken automatically, never filed and never used as a replacement. It stays in the release list with a warning, and a finished download stops with the problem "The title does not fit the movie", where you can file it anyway. A whole title with more words after it, and a name only TMDB or Radarr know as a translation or alternative title, count only with the movie's year in the name.
sections.where: Title page › Search, and Downloads › Problems

sections.title: Why nothing was loaded
sections.body: After an automatic search each version says how many releases fit and, by reason, why the rest were refused. The same for series seasons and albums, in the log too.

sections.title: Replaced files in the recycle bin
sections.body: A file an upgrade replaces now stands in the recycle bin like a deleted one and comes back with one click. If its title has left the library since, restoring adds the title again, unwatched. When a file cannot go back to its place, the row says why: something lies there, the version has another file by now, or a Radarr, Sonarr or Lidarr connection feeds the version.
sections.where: Settings › Folders and naming › Recycle folder

sections.title: A broken archive counts as a failed download
sections.body: When a finished download misses archive volumes or wants a password, nexcrate treats it like a download its client gave up on: the release is blocked, its files are thrown away, and a replacement is searched. Removing a finished download that was never filed now deletes its job folder too, and only that folder.

small: Large imports, takeovers and new artists are written in parts, so other programs no longer wait minutes for the database. If it is busy all the same, they get 503 with a Retry-After.
A replacement after a failure goes first in the indexers' request budget, but never past a limit an indexer has made known.
A version shows the release its file came from.
Posters come from TMDB when the source cannot deliver one.
Saving the size table names the quality and the field that is wrong.
The automatic search no longer takes box sets for a studio album; deluxe and expanded editions still fit.
Titles in your language stay when a Radarr import runs.
A takeover no longer gives a file that already belongs to one version to a second one.
release.nex follows a file into the recycle bin and back.

0.3.1.lead: This version files downloads whose files arrive later, from a seedbox for example, and fits the library on a phone.

sections.title: Files that arrive later
sections.body: When a sync brings the files to the server only after the download finished, from a seedbox for example, the download used to stay behind as a problem because nexcrate could not find the files. nexcrate now looks again every few minutes for two days and files it once the folder is complete and no longer changes.

sections.title: Choose the folder yourself
sections.body: When nexcrate cannot find a download and has nothing to propose, you can now choose its folder yourself, for movies too. nexcrate derives the mapping for the download client from it and files the download right away. "Try again" is now also offered beside a proposal.

small: The library is no longer wider than the screen on a phone.
Searching while the automatic searches the same series now shows that search instead of an error.

0.3.2.lead: This version assigns more music files by itself and lets you choose tracks only the target release of an album has.

sections.title: Tracks only the target release has
sections.body: Once files of a download lie in the album folder, its release is fixed. A bonus track only the album's target release has could then not be assigned. "Assign by hand" now offers such tracks in a group of their own, and the file is named after the target release.

small: Scene style file names like "01-artist_name-title" are read without the artist, so the title fits.
Credits like "(Produced By …)" or "(ft. …)" in a title no longer get in the way of the assignment.

0.3.3.lead: This version waits for downloads whose folder a sync creates before the files are in it.

sections.title: Downloads from a seedbox, second part
sections.body: A sync tool like Resilio or Syncthing often creates the folder first and keeps unfinished files under a temporary name. nexcrate then met a folder without a video or music and stopped for good. It now keeps looking for two days, as it already did for a missing folder, and files the download once the files are there and the folder has stopped changing. The card offers "Try again" as well.

small: The card of a download without video or music now says that nexcrate keeps looking, instead of only telling you to remove it.

0.3.4.lead: This version lets the assistant create a profile again, and reads series folders that were added on the movie side.

sections.title: Profiles from the assistant
sections.body: On the last page, the assistant showed "This does not exist, or not any more" for a new profile under Profiles, and Save stayed locked. It built its overview for a version, and such a profile belongs to none yet. It now builds the overview for the kind of the profile, and you can save it.

sections.title: Series folders on the movie side
sections.body: A folder of series added under Movies was read as movies: every season folder became a movie of its own and stayed unknown. The folder now says when it holds season folders, and a folder you added can be read as a series folder with one click.

small: When TMDB stops answering during a scan, the job says so with the reason, instead of leaving the rest unknown without a word.

0.4.0.lead: This version takes the indexers from Prowlarr and keeps them up to date, gives every torrent a seeding goal, and clears finished torrents from the download client once the goal is reached.

sections.title: Indexers from Prowlarr
sections.body: Enter Prowlarr once with its address and API key. nexcrate takes every indexer from it, searches through Prowlarr and syncs on saving, on a click and every 15 minutes. What you change, add or delete in Prowlarr arrives by itself. There is nothing to set up in Prowlarr.

sections.title: Seeding goals per indexer
sections.body: Every torrent indexer can carry a ratio, a seed time and a seed time of its own for season packs. They come from Prowlarr, along with an import from Radarr, Sonarr or Lidarr, or from you. qBittorrent, Transmission and Deluge get the goal when the torrent is added.

sections.title: Removing finished torrents
sections.body: Once a torrent is imported and has reached its goal, nexcrate removes it together with its files in the download folder. The file in the library stays. The switch is on for new download clients and off for existing ones after the update.

small: When qBittorrent removes torrents by a rule of its own, the download client's card says so.
An indexer switched off in Prowlarr shows as switched off in a search instead of failing.
Minimum seeders now go up to 1000.
